lab_questions.title: External API Failures & Sagas (Rollbacks)
lab_questions.description: Evaluate a candidate's ability to maintain data integrity when interfacing with external services. The lab covers database transactions, atomic blocks, request deduplication (idempotency), and fault tolerance via retries.
lab_questions.startup_command: python manage.py migrate && python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8010

tasks.title: Transaction Atomicity & Rollbacks
tasks.description:
Buying a stock involves deducting the wallet balance, then calling the NASDAQ API. `POST /api/orders/buy/` deducts the balance and commits *before* making the HTTP request. If the NASDAQ API times out, the user loses their money but gets no stock.

**Goal:** Wrap the entire operation in `transaction.atomic()`. If the `requests.post()` to the external exchange raises a `Timeout` or `RequestException`, raise an exception (or rollback manually) so the database rolls back the wallet deduction automatically, preventing financial loss.

tasks.title: Idempotent Order Deduplication
tasks.description:
Users on slow connections frequently double-click the 'Buy' button, causing the API to receive duplicate requests. This results in users being double-charged and double-credited with stock.

**Goal:** The frontend now sends a unique `idempotency_key` in the payload. Check if a `StockOrder` with this `idempotency_key` already exists. If it does, return `200 OK` (with the existing order details) and skip the deduction and external API call entirely.

tasks.title: Fault Tolerance & Connection Retries
tasks.description:
The external stock exchange API is notoriously flaky, occasionally dropping connections (`ConnectionError`). Currently, a single dropped connection completely fails the user's order.

**Goal:** Implement a retry mechanism for the `requests.post()` call. If a `ConnectionError` occurs, the system should retry the request up to a total of 3 attempts before finally failing and rolling back.
